description: Story 1.1 - Hide Banned/Suspended Users Across Platform: Add query-level author status filtering to all public endpoints that return posts (feed, explore, single post, user posts, saved posts, featured content). The User model has status field with enum ['active', 'banned', 'suspended']. The authGuard already blocks banned/suspended users from making authenticated requests, but PUBLIC endpoints using optionalAuth do NOT filter posts by author status. Posts from banned/suspended authors must be excluded at the database query level.
steps: Step 1: Modify backend/src/modules/posts/post.service.js - getFeed() function: After the existing query construction (line ~55), add a filter to exclude posts whose authorId references a banned or suspended user. Since Post.find() uses cursor-based pagination and populates authorId, the most efficient approach is to: (a) First get the list of banned/suspended user IDs, then add { authorId: { $nin: bannedUserIds } } to the query. Import the User model at the top. Add a helper function getBannedUserIds() that queries User.find({ status: { $in: ['banned', 'suspended'] } }).select('_id').lean() and returns the IDs. Call this before the Post.find() query and add the $nin filter to the query object.

Step 2: Modify backend/src/modules/posts/post.service.js - getSinglePost() function: After fetching the post and checking if it exists, add a check: if (post.authorId && post.authorId.status) is not needed since we don't populate status. Instead, after the populate, look up the author's status. The simplest approach: change the populate to include 'status' in the select fields: .populate('authorId', 'username avatarUrl role isVerified verifiedType status'). Then after the post is fetched, check if post.authorId.status is 'banned' or 'suspended' and if so throw a 404 error (post not found) so banned authors' posts appear to not exist.

Step 3: Modify backend/src/modules/users/user.service.js - getUserPosts() function: Add the same banned author filtering. Since this fetches posts for a specific userId, we need to check if that user is banned/suspended. Import User model (already imported). Before querying posts, fetch the target user's status. If the user is banned or suspended, return empty results (data: [], meta with zeros). This ensures viewing a banned user's profile shows no posts.

Step 4: Modify backend/src/modules/users/user.service.js - getSavedPosts() function: After fetching posts by IDs, filter out posts whose authorId (populated) has status 'banned' or 'suspended'. Change the Post.find populate to include 'status': .populate('authorId', 'username avatarUrl role isVerified verifiedType status'). Then filter: posts = posts.filter(p => p.authorId && p.authorId.status === 'active').

Step 5: Modify backend/src/modules/admin/config.routes.js - GET /featured endpoint: After filtering out null posts, add a filter to exclude posts where the populated authorId has status 'banned' or 'suspended'. The authorId is already populated with '_id username avatarUrl'. Add 'status' to the populate select. Then filter: data = data.filter(post => post.authorId && post.authorId.status === 'active').
acceptance_criteria: getFeed() excludes posts from banned/suspended authors at the database query level
getSinglePost() returns 404 for posts by banned/suspended authors
getUserPosts() returns empty results when the target user is banned/suspended
getSavedPosts() filters out posts by banned/suspended authors from results
GET /config/featured filters out posts by banned/suspended authors
When a user's status changes back to 'active', their posts automatically reappear (no manual intervention needed since filtering is dynamic)
All changes use status === 'active' check (positive check) rather than hardcoding banned/suspended (future-proof)
verification: Verify User model import is present in post.service.js
Verify the getBannedUserIds helper function or equivalent filtering logic exists
findings: All three files pass node --check syntax validation. The NODE_OPTIONS env var needed to be cleared to run node --check in this sandbox. Implementation follows existing patterns (populate with select, .filter(), Object.assign for errors). The getInactiveUserIds helper is inside the cached getFeed callback so that cache invalidation on user status changes works correctly.
